articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The first hurricane of the Atlantic season was forecast to intensify rapidly and cause dangerous conditions in the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and southern Mississippi when it makes landfall late Friday or early Saturday.
articles.title: Isaias strengthens into Category 2 hurricane on collision course with the Gulf Coast

articles.author: Huo Jingnan
articles.description: The company says Russian operatives used its AI chatbot to update their bosses, shedding light on influence campaigns previously not attributed to Russia.
articles.title: OpenAI caught Russians and Iranians using ChatGPT for influence campaigns

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier has returned home after a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea supporting the Iran war. The extended deployment drew attention following reports of crew stress and supply shortages.
articles.title: The long-deployed USS Lincoln returns home to San Diego Bay

articles.author: Rodney Carmichael
articles.description: NPR Music culture critic and reporter Rodney Carmichael ruminates on the latest in rap culture. This week: an unbothered, radically different, equal but opposite response to rap's podcast bros.
articles.title: Discursive Verses: Vic Mensa and the rise of a rap manosphere counterculture

articles.author: Michel Martin
articles.description: NPR's Michel Martin hosted a panel conversation about mental health and suicide in the Black community, exploring a difficult subject in deeply personal conversations.
articles.title: Suicide is up among Black Americans. We need to talk about it.

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln is returning home to San Diego Thursday after supporting the Iran war during a record long deployment of 265 uninterrupted days at sea that included reports of deteriorating conditions among its crew.
articles.title: The long-deployed USS Lincoln is returning home to San Diego

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: U.S. authorities added new torture charges to their case against former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, ramping up pressure on the ousted authoritarian leader already fighting drug trafficking allegations.
articles.title: New U.S. indictment charges former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro with torture

articles.author: Russell Lewis
articles.description: Four people — two NASA astronauts, one from the European Space Agency and a Russian cosmonaut — spent nearly eight months at the space station, conducting spacewalks, science experiments and research.
articles.title: 4 people on NASA's Crew-12 mission return to Earth after 8 months in space

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The South Korean announcement on Thursday came days after its President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified punitive steps if Ukraine refuses to apologize over the revelation.
articles.title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW dispute

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow (now); Hamish Mackay and Adam Fulton (earlier)
articles.description:
Sagal Abdi-Wali defeats Green party leader Zack Polanski to retain the Holborn and St Pancras seat for Labour

Labour fends off Green party to win Holborn and St Pancras byelection

Activists in Camden have suggested the Greens’ decision to back the anti-Zionism motion has cost them votes in the byelection.
Councillors for both Labour the Liberal Democrats told the Press Association that voters had informed them they would not be backing the Green party after it passed the motion last weekend calling Zionism racism.
It is clear now we will come a close second in this by-election. Taking the fight to Labour in one of its safest seats shows just how far the Greens have come.
Voters want us to keep Labour’s feet to the fire on affordable housing, public ownership of water and the climate crisis. Greens will be there every single day, holding Labour to account and demanding the change people voted for.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour wins Holborn and St Pancras byelection; Polanski ‘absolutely’ intends to remain Green party leader – UK politics live

articles.author: Denis Campbell
articles.description:
Decision by Royal College of Pharmacy to end sponsorship comes after concerns over Teva Pharmaceuticals’ ‘activities’
A second major UK health body has cut ties with an Israeli drug firm after coming under pressure from pro-Palestine campaigners.
The Royal College of Pharmacy has dropped Teva UK, the British arm of the global medicines producer Teva Pharmaceuticals, as a sponsor of and exhibitor at its annual conference next month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Second UK health body drops Israeli drug firm after activist pressure

articles.author: Rachel Salvidge
articles.description:
Exclusive: Firms made more than £340m last year from processing industrial and commercial wastewater at sewage works that are unable to remove many chemical pollutants
Water companies in the UK made more than £340m in revenue last year by pouring billions of litres of industrial and commercial wastewater into sewage treatment works that experts say are not designed to remove most chemicals, leaving pollutants to pass into rivers, seas and farmland.
Water companies are required by law to take industrial wastewater and issue permits called “trade-effluent consents” that allow businesses to send it to sewage works, though water companies can refuse applications.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Revealed: the ‘black box’ wastewater trade that rakes in millions for UK utility companies

articles.author: Jonathan Barrett  and Josh Taylor
articles.description:
The $11-a-share offer would have been the biggest debut on the stock market since the telecommunication giant in 1997

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Firmus Technologies has scrapped what was set to be Australia’s biggest company listing in decades after investor demand for its much-hyped AI datacentre business failed to materialise.
A Firmus spokesperson said the board decided that proceeding with the offer was no longer in the best interests of the company and its shareholders.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Firmus pulls biggest ASX float since Telstra amid investor doubt about datacentre company

articles.author: Saher Ahmed in Cairo
articles.description:
Matsadaash staff allege torture and forced confessions after being held on charges of working for Muslim Brotherhood
Egyptian journalists are planning a new protest in Cairo this weekend after six colleagues were charged with terrorism offences amid allegations they had been tortured in police detention.
Last week, Egyptian authorities arrested the journalists, from the independent factchecking and investigative platform Matsadaash, accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and producing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest over detention of six colleagues

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
Species with leaves large enough to be seen from space is already critically endangered – and plans are afoot to protect it
A chance social media encounter has led to the race-against-time discovery of a new species of giant waterlily that has until now been hidden in the depths of Colombia’s jungle.
But the plant, which is so huge it is visible from space, is already considered critically endangered.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How a plant selfie in Colombian jungle led to ‘jaw dropping’ giant waterlily find

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Saudi Arabia has not commented on claims, but confirmed three killed in airport strikes earlier this week
Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis say they have struck Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh ⁠airport with a ballistic missile, badly damaging a plane and leading some airlines to suspend flights to the capital.
The group provided no evidence, and Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the claim.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Houthis claim attack on Riyadh airport as airlines suspend flights to Saudi capital

articles.author: Sammy Gecsoyler
articles.description:
Victory by Sagal Abdi-Wali in north London seat will be a relief for Andy Burnham in high-stakes battle for the left of British politics

Holborn and St Pancras byelection – live updates


Labour has seen off the Greens to win the Holborn and St Pancras byelection in a result that will relieve Andy Burnham and dent Zack Polanski’s position as a decisive power player on the left of British politics.
The byelection, called after former prime minister Keir Starmer resigned from the seat in September, was considered a two-horse race between the Labour candidate, Sagal Abdi-Wali, and the Green party leader, Polanski. Abdi-Wali received 12,292 votes, 45% of the vote, to Polanski’s 8,928, 33% of the vote.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour fends off Green party to win Holborn and St Pancras byelection

articles.author: Penry Buckley
articles.description:
State planning minister declares project ‘state significant’, wresting approval process away from local council
Plans for a grand new public square in the centre of Sydney are in doubt after the New South Wales planning minister declared the project “state significant”, wresting the approval process away from the City of Sydney.
The lord mayor, Clover Moore, released renders in August for the plaza opposite Sydney’s town hall. The design for the space, which the council had expected to be completed by 2031, include a semi-circular clearing projecting eastwards towards Hyde park, with a fountain and a grove of native trees.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Plans for Sydney’s controversial new public square in doubt after NSW government intervention

articles.author: Robert Mackey (now); Uwa Ede-Osifo, Shrai Popat, Maya Yang and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
Pentagon chief joins Trump in attempt to use deadly shooting at Texas base to attack former Democratic president

Thousands turn out to welcome weary USS Lincoln sailors

Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Donald Trump has urged James Talarico, the Democratic nominee in the US Senate race in Texas, to debate Ken Paxton – Republican attorney general that the president has endorsed in the election.
On Truth Social, Trump described Paxton as “ready, willing, and able” to take on Talarico – the 37-year-old state representative who has been leading in several polls.
In Georgia, Jon Ossoff, the Democratic incumbent will face off against Mike Collins – a congressman and the Trump-backed Republican nominee at 7pm ET.
At the same time in Michigan, progressive insurgent Abdul El-Sayed, will debate Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee also endorsed by the president.
Finally, it’s the second debate in Maine in as many days. Susan Collins, the five-term Republican incumbent will spar (again) with the Democratic nominee, Troy Jackson, at 8pm ET.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth falsely claims Obama called 2009 Fort Hood attack ‘workplace violence’ – US politics live

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Thousands expected to march in Delhi on Saturday, as anger mounts over controversial changes to voter lists in world’s largest democracy 
India’s Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which began as a satirical movement but is now emerging as a political force among gen Z’s, says authorities have begun detaining its members en masse days before a major anti-government protest in Delhi.
Opposition parties, their student units, and the “Cockroach” youth movement have been holding almost daily demonstrations seeking the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a controversial revision of ⁠voter lists.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s ‘Cockroach’ party accuses government of mass detention of members ahead of weekend protest

articles.author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles and Lex McMenamin in New York
articles.description:
Police say man taken to hospital and mayor says child physically unharmed as he condemns ‘unconscionable’ act
A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot and injured a man in New York City on Thursday afternoon during an enforcement operation, federal officials said.
The man was conscious and hospitalized, authorities said, and the shooting quickly sparked angry protests from local residents and elected officials in the neighborhood.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ICE agent shoots man in New York City with five-year-old reportedly in car

articles.author: Anna Betts
articles.description:
Residents in areas from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Florida urged to ‘evacuate if told to do so’
Millions of people from Louisiana to Florida were under hurricane warnings on Thursday as Hurricane Isaias heads toward the US Gulf coast, with weather officials warning of dangerous storm surge, hurricane-force winds, heavy rainfall and flooding.
Isaias intensified from a tropical storm into the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season on Wednesday night, and has prompted state of emergency declarations in Florida, Alabama and Georgia, as well as evacuation orders and school closures in several Florida counties as officials urge residents to prepare for its arrival.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Millions on alert as Hurricane Isaias set to bring dangerous storm surge

articles.author: Dee Jefferson
articles.description:
Making its southern hemisphere debut, Dance Reflections will feature collaborators of Rosalía, Madonna and Beyoncé – and a high-wire takeover of the Cutaway

Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

A “once-in-a-lifetime” program of dance works of scale will be coming to Sydney in January, including 11 international works from France, Belgium, South Africa and beyond making their Australian premiere.
The program, which triples the scale of the dance offering at the last Sydney festival, will bring 174 performers and crew to Sydney, with the crowning jewel being the acclaimed French choreographer Rachid Ouramdane’s Outsider. The 2024 work features 21 dancers from the Ballet du Grand Théâtre de Genève and four elite athletes, navigating a “cat’s cradle” of high wires and slack lines, to the mesmerising, minimalist music of the avant garde composer Julius Eastman.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sydney festival 2027: 11 international dance works to headline ‘once-in-a-lifetime’ program

articles.author: Tess Ikonomou
articles.description:
Treasurer earmarks funds for year-long transition period for tax office, delaying ban’s 30 November start date

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A controversial ban on credit card payments on tax bills will be delayed by more than six months, after the federal government overruled the tax office and announced new stopgap funding.
The treasurer, Jim Chalmers, announced extra funding on Friday, after days of criticism and calls from small business to halt the ban.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jim Chalmers overrules ATO’s controversial ban on credit card payments following business outcry

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Nidal Hasan, army psychiatrist who killed 13 people, will be executed by firing squad on 3 December
Pete Hegseth has said the execution of Nidal Hasan, the former army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, will be a public event when the sentence is carried out later this year. A defense department official later confirmed the execution will be livestreamed.
In an interview with Real America’s Voice, the Pentagon secretary said the firing squad will carry out the sentence at Fort Hood, Texas, at 1pm on Thursday, 3 December. This would be the first US military execution in more than 60 years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pentagon says execution of Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed

articles.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
articles.description:
Peter Fonagy lauds courage of young people and warns of consequences of rising prevalence of mental illness

Full report | NHS at risk of ‘system failures’ as demand for ADHD and autism care soars, inquiry finds

Explainer | What has the Fonagy review found and what does it recommend?

Eighteen months ago, in an off-the-cuff remark during a discussion on disability benefit cuts, Wes Streeting said mental health conditions were being “overdiagnosed”, riding headlong into another culture war.
He later apologised for the comment, but at the time it seemed the then health secretary had endorsed a populist view that ordinary stresses and disappointments had become too often medicalised, resulting in a surge of bogus clinical diagnoses and creating a “snowflake generation” of fragile, avoidant and workshy young people.
I am in awe of their courage. Young people are contending with more powerful forces than I ever faced
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No ‘snowflakes’: mental health review says today’s youth have it harder and harms are real

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Flowers, tried six times over 1996 murders of four people, faced execution before supreme court tossed his conviction
Curtis Flowers, a Black man who spent more than 22 years in prison and was on death row in Mississippi before the US supreme court threw out his conviction and death sentence, has died. He was 56.
Flowers’ family confirmed that he died on Wednesday at his home in Mississippi, attorney Rob McDuff told the Associated Press on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Curtis Flowers, US man wrongfully imprisoned for 22 years, dies aged 56

articles.author: Jon Henley in Paris
articles.description:
Education minister promises 3,000 substitute teachers by Tuesday with schools still blockaded across France
High school students have again blockaded schools and marched through cities across France, promising to continue their campaign against the poor state of the national education system in the 10th day of protests that have left hundreds injured.
Large crowds took to the streets on Thursday for mainly peaceful demonstrations in cities including Lille, Rennes, Nantes, Lyon, Toulon and Marseille, while in Paris a large procession marched through the city centre to the Place de la Bastille.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: French ministers scramble to appease students after 10 days of protests

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
The brothers’ parents, Martin and Debra Robinson, to address court before a Mexican judge hands down verdict
A Mexican judge is expected to hand down his verdict in the high-profile murder trial of three men accused of killing two Australian surfers and their American friend in 2024.
Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33 respectively, and their friend Carter Rhoad, 30, were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast when they were shot dead in Baja California state in an alleged robbery.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Men accused of shooting Australian surfer brothers and US friend dead in Mexico to learn fate as trial concludes

articles.author: South West News Service
articles.description:
Free-roaming Aldabra population far exceeds human population of Seychelles after decades-long recovery programme
A survey of the world’s largest free-roaming giant tortoise population has discovered that the once endangered species is thriving.
A population of Aldabra giant tortoises lives on an island in Seychelles called Aldabra Atoll.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scientists discover 180,000 giant tortoises on one Seychelles island

articles.author: Sam Jones and Ashifa Kassam in Madrid
articles.description:
Rally to remember woman, 87, whose rent battle with investment firm triggered nationwide protests over housing crisis
About 20,000 people took part in a march through the centre of Madrid on Thursday evening in memory of María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her flat in the capital a fortnight before her death triggered mass protests over Spain’s housing crisis.
The pensioner, whose flat had been bought by an investment firm that sought to increase her rent by 230%, had become the public face of the crisis before her death in hospital on Wednesday night.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thousands march in Madrid after death of evicted pensioner Maricarmen

articles.author: Victoria Bekiempis
articles.description:
Ousted Venezuelan president and Cilia Flores have been in jail in New York since early January
The deposed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, have been indicted for alleged conspiracy to commit torture, according to Manhattan federal court papers unsealed on Thursday.
The superseding indictment was unsealed shortly before Flores appeared at court in her ongoing push for pretrial release – which was denied by Judge Alvin Hellerstein. Maduro and Flores have been jailed in New York City since early January.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nicolás Maduro and his wife indicted for alleged torture of US citizens

articles.author: Donna Lu
articles.description:
Intense flash of radio waves is more than 10bn years old and has travelled through ‘approximately 80% of cosmic history’
A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away, a mysterious flash of energy was released into the universe.
Astronomers have now detected that flash – a burst of radio waves which travelled for more than 10bn years before reaching Earth – what they believe to be the most distant fast radio burst (FRB) ever recorded.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Astronomers detect mysterious burst of energy from a galaxy far, far away

articles.author: Louisa Loveluck
articles.description:
Embassies post links to hastily produced online film echoing style of real Guardian documentary about mass killings of Gaza civilians
The Israeli government is promoting an online film project that mimics the style of NAZA, the award-winning documentary that details Israel’s mass killings of civilians in Gaza, in an attempt to counter the real film’s findings.
The real documentary, directed by the Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, and produced by the Guardian, is in cinemas and will be shown in more than 50 countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel promotes film that mimics NAZA documentary

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Consulate targeted in sanctions spat has unusual diplomatic status that clashes with Israel’s ambitions to fully annex the city
Israel’s attempt to close the British consulate general in Jerusalem was primarily designed to deter London from imposing sanctions on settlements in occupied Palestine. But it also served the current government’s ambitions to fully annex Jerusalem as a national capital, diplomatic and legal experts said.
The UK mission to the city has an unusual diplomatic status, which dates back to before the founding of the state of Israel, rooted in a vision of Jerusalem as a neutral enclave under international control.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel’s downgrading of UK consulate aims to tighten its hold on Jerusalem

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
UK and Israel back away from full diplomatic confrontation, though British presence in Palestine will be much reduced
Israel and the UK have backed away from a full-scale diplomatic confrontation, with Britain announcing it is rebranding its consulate general ⁠building in ⁠East Jerusalem ​as a UK mission, a move that will result in UK diplomats leaving Israel, with only seven to remain in the building. Among those leaving is the consul general, Helen Winterton.
The change was forced on the UK by the Israeli government as punishment for the decision by the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, last month to ban trade with illegal settlements and introduce a tougher sanctions regime against those who aided the building of settlements. The UK is seeking to protect the two-state solution as the best means of ending the Israel-Palestine conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British consulate in East Jerusalem will stay open as UK mission, says Ed Miliband

articles.author: Rachel Savage and agencies
articles.description:
Government forces’ attack raises risk of internal conflict in Ethiopia that could trigger regional war 
Eritrean troops who crossed into Ethiopia’s Tigray region have come under drone attack from government forces, raising the risk that renewed internal conflict in Ethiopia could trigger an all-out regional war between the neighbouring countries.
Military vehicles carrying soldiers drove across Eritrea’s southern border into Tigray on Wednesday, reaching the town of Adigrat 25 miles (40km) south, according to civilian witnesses, a militia commander and the conflict monitoring group Acled.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ethiopia launches drone attack against Eritrean troops who crossed into Tigray

articles.author: Jakub Krupa and Martin Belam
articles.description:
Two men arrested last night as security patrols near RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire found an abandoned vehicle and a breach in the fence
in Athens
Over in Athens, Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, has been forced, yet again, to address allegations of misconduct by Kimberly Guilfoyle, America’s ambassador to Greece. 
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two Latvian men arrested for trespass offences at RAF airbase – as it happened

articles.author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
articles.description:
Parviz Sabeti denies allegations he led Savak intelligence agency under shah and directed torture of thousands
The alleged “chief torturer” for the deposed Shah of Iran is a step closer to trial for human rights abuses after a Florida federal judge rejected his demand to halt a lawsuit brought by three former political prisoners.
Parviz Sabeti, who was reported last year to have lived in a quiet upscale central Florida community, is accused of being the former head of Savak, the shah’s secret police and intelligence agency. The plaintiffs say they discovered his whereabouts only after a photo of Sabeti at a 2023 protest against the Iranian government was posted on social media by his daughter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Florida judge allows lawsuit against Shah of Iran’s alleged ‘chief torturer’ to move forward

articles.author: Emma Loffhagen and Leyland Cecco in Toronto
articles.description:
Most prestigious literature prize goes to Canadian known for genre-crossing works such as Autobiography of Red

‘Delights await!’: Margaret Atwood and other writers on Nobel winner Anne Carson

Where to start with: Anne Carson

The Nobel prize in literature has been awarded to the Canadian poet and essayist Anne Carson, the Swedish Academy has announced.
The academy cited the author’s “bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Anne Carson wins Nobel prize in literature 2026

articles.author: Luke Harding
articles.description:
Zelenskyy says Kremlin deliberately targeted ‘ordinary public transport stop’ in Kramatorsk, with 18 wounded

A Russian missile strike on a bus in the eastern city of Kramatorsk has killed at least 30 people, officials have said, in one of the worst attacks by Moscow on Ukrainian civilians this year.
The regional prosecutor’s office in the Donetsk region said on Thursday the vehicle had been hit at 10am by an aerial bomb. “As of now, the death toll from this morning’s attack has risen to 30. Eighteen people were wounded,” it said, adding that all local public transport had been suspended.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russian attack on bus kills at least 30 people near Ukraine frontline

articles.author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
articles.description:
Parties vow to challenge law in court, arguing that extra reward for those with 42% of support distorts public representation

Europe live – latest updates

A controversial overhaul to electoral law that critics say is aimed at boosting Giorgia Meloni’s chances of clinging on to power in elections next year has been given final approval by the Italian parliament.
Meloni, the Italian prime minister, says the new system, which introduces a fully proportional model, including bonus seats for any coalition that wins the most votes, will bring about greater political stability, while opposition parties argue that it mainly serves the interests of those in power.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Italian opposition cries foul as Meloni’s electoral reform passed in secret ballot

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Responding to a Guardian report that revealed thousands of tonnes of fuel was transported to Russia, Seoul said it was investigating the cases
South Korea will take legal action if it finds that shipments of fuel from its ports to Russia broke domestic law, the government has said, responding to a Guardian report on the trade.
The government, in a statement issued by the foreign and trade ministries and the customs service, said that it is “checking additional information concerning the loading cases reported by the Guardian” and “if the verification establishes that our laws and regulations have been violated, it plans to act in accordance with the law”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South Korea threatens legal action if fuel shipments to Russia found to have broken law

articles.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
articles.description:
Investigators probe Asahi, Kirin, Suntory and Sapporo breweries – which together control more than 90% of Japan’s beer market
Japanese authorities have raided the country’s four biggest breweries over suspicions they colluded to set the price of beer and other beverages – a practice media reports said could have forced drinkers to pay over the odds.
Officials from the Fair Trade Commission this week searched the offices of Asahi Breweries, Kirin Brewery, Suntory Beer and Sapporo Breweries – which together control more than 90% of the domestic market. The quartet are suspected of violating the anti-monopoly law.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japan beer giants raided over suspicions they colluded to set the price of beverages

articles.author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok and agencies
articles.description:
NGOs in Indonesian Borneo file class action lawsuit calling for government to better manage annual fires and 
The Indonesian government has been accused of “gross negligence” in a class action lawsuit over its handling of wildfires that have cloaked large parts of South-east Asia in a toxic haze, shuttered schools and caused a spike in respiratory illnesses.
The lawsuit, filed by indigenous and civil society groups in the Indonesian part of Borneo, named President Prabowo Subianto and the governor of West Kalimantan among 10 defendants. The case seeks comprehensive recovery and rehabilitation measures that would include covering the healthcare costs of residents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indonesia accused of ‘gross negligence’ in wildfires lawsuit as haze tests region

articles.author: Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
Inquest under way into why President Lula’s success in curbing Amazon deforestation has not led to success at polls 
More fire, more ash, more crime, more death. And a globally important ecosystem driven ever more rapidly towards a point of no return. That is the prospect for the Amazon rainforest for at least the next four years if Flávio Bolsonaro holds on to the lead he established this week in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election.
This appears to be of far more concern to the outside world than to voters in Latin America’s biggest, richest and most biodiverse nation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro’s advance in Brazil’s election is grim jolt for climate campaigners

articles.author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok
articles.description:
New ‘support and training centre’ prompts concern in region but China says it is ‘not directed at any third party’ 
Satellite images show attack jets stationed at a new Chinese military facility in Laos, which opened last week and gives Beijing’s air force its first foothold in mainland south-east Asia.
Images provided by the commercial satellite provider Vantor show eight light attack aircraft positioned at Ban Keun airport alongside what appear to be more than a dozen military vehicles lined up in rows.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Satellite images show attack jets at Chinese military facility in Laos

articles.author: Eva Corlett in Auckland and Adeshola Ore in Melbourne
articles.description:
Hamam al-Hammami spent 175 days in New Zealand until May 2019, as Australian Jewish group calls for full investigation into his time in Melbourne
New Zealand authorities have launched their own investigation into the flydubai co-pilot who allegedly tried to hijack an Israel-bound plane, after police confirmed he underwent flight training there about a year after he abandoned a degree in Australia.
Disaster was narrowly averted on 30 September when passengers and crew intervened to stop the alleged attempt of the co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, 29, to take control of a flight to Tel Aviv with 182 people onboard.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flydubai attack investigation widens as alleged hijacker’s training in New Zealand scrutinised

articles.author: Rachel Savage and agencies
articles.description:
Health minister says 28 contacts identified after death of citizen who arrived from DRC on Saturday
Kenya has reported its first-ever Ebola death, the health minister announced on Tuesday, as the disease continues to spread rapidly through the north-east of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where the outbreak was announced in May.
This is the 17th outbreak of the highly infectious, often deadly disease in the DRC. As of 2 October, 4,082 people had died out of 8,463 confirmed cases in the country since the emergence of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, for which there is still no vaccine nor specific treatment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kenya confirms first Ebola case as virus ‘surges’ in DR Congo province

articles.author: Lucy Kassa
articles.description:
Civilians try to flee as men and boys rounded up on streets by new alliance as Ethiopia conflict erupts again
As renewed fighting has threatened a fresh humanitarian crisis in the northern region of Ethiopia, reports are emerging that a new alliance of armed groups in Tigray has been forcibly recruiting men and boys to its ranks.
Renewed conflict erupted on 23 September between Ethiopia’s federal government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which rules the region, shattering the fragile Pretoria peace agreement signed between the two sides in November 2022.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tigray rebel groups ‘forcibly recruiting boys as young as 15’ as fighting spreads

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Pakistani authorities insist marchers calling for former PM to be released from jail will not reach the capital
Imran Khan’s supporters have begun a march to Islamabad to demand his release from jail after efforts by the government to halt the protest failed.
The march began in the former prime minister’s stronghold province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in north-west Pakistan on Sunday, according to leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Supporters of Imran Khan start march on locked-down Islamabad

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Mumbai
articles.description:
Thousands gather in Mumbai with heavy police presence as concerns mount that millions will be denied voting rights
India’s youth-led Cockroach movement kicked off more nationwide protests on Friday as thousands of people gathered in Mumbai, amid mounting concerns that millions of citizens are being unfairly stripped of their vote.
The movement, which calls itself the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) and has massive support among the country’s gen Zs, returned to the streets to demand the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach movement launches new protests over changes to voter roll

articles.author: Megan Davies and James Michelin for MetDesk
articles.description:
Up to 300mm of rain could fall in places, while extreme downpours bring landslides and deaths in Nepal
Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.
Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, are most at risk. Valencia has experienced several damaging floods in recent years. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Eastern Spain braces for torrential rain and flooding

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up ‘passengers would lose their lives’
The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a “last push” to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life.
Capt Smit Machchhar, who was recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described to India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, how he helped save the plane and its more than 170 passengers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I was fighting for my life’: Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls flydubai cockpit attack

articles.author: Rachel Leingang, George Chidi and Austin Byrdsell
articles.description:
Candidates traded personal attacks and clashed over a range of issues in closely watched US Senate debates on Thursday, with control of Congress at stake
With just weeks left in the contentious midterm election campaign, candidates in a trio of highly-competitive Senate races debated Thursday night, clashing over the economy, tariffs, the Iran war and abortion rights, with control of the upper chamber at stake.
In Georgia, incumbent Democratic senator Jon Ossoff faced GOP representative Mike Collins. In Michigan, Democrat Abdul Al-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers debated over the state’s open Senate seat. And in Maine, longtime senator Susan Collins met Democratic challenger Troy Jackson. Democrats need to flip four Republican-held Senate seats to win the majority.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US midterms: key takeaways from Senate debates in Michigan, Georgia and Maine

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland, with David Nir, produced by Danielle Stephens and Nada Smiljanic with executive producer Phil Maynard
articles.description:
Polling out this week suggests the Democrats could do something no one thought possible even a few months ago: take back the US Senate. Despite this, Donald Trump is telling crowds at rallies across the country that the Republicans will ‘win big’.
This week, Jonathan Freedland speaks to David Nir of the Downballot about why Democrats are feeling so hopeful in deep red states
Watch Jonathan Freedland on our new Politics Weekly YouTube channel
Send your questions and feedback to politicsweeklyamerica@theguardian.com
Watch Aditya Chakrabortty’s new series, Radical Thinking, on YouTube, or listen to it on the Politics Weekly feed
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is a ‘blue tsunami’ going to wipe out Republicans? – podcast

articles.author: Robert Mackey (now); Uwa Ede-Osifo, Shrai Popat, Maya Yang and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
Pentagon chief joins Trump in attempt to use deadly shooting at Texas base to attack former Democratic president

Thousands turn out to welcome weary USS Lincoln sailors

Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Donald Trump has urged James Talarico, the Democratic nominee in the US Senate race in Texas, to debate Ken Paxton – Republican attorney general that the president has endorsed in the election.
On Truth Social, Trump described Paxton as “ready, willing, and able” to take on Talarico – the 37-year-old state representative who has been leading in several polls.
In Georgia, Jon Ossoff, the Democratic incumbent will face off against Mike Collins – a congressman and the Trump-backed Republican nominee at 7pm ET.
At the same time in Michigan, progressive insurgent Abdul El-Sayed, will debate Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee also endorsed by the president.
Finally, it’s the second debate in Maine in as many days. Susan Collins, the five-term Republican incumbent will spar (again) with the Democratic nominee, Troy Jackson, at 8pm ET.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth falsely claims Obama called 2009 Fort Hood attack ‘workplace violence’ – US politics live

articles.author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles and Lex McMenamin in New York
articles.description:
Police say man taken to hospital and mayor says child physically unharmed as he condemns ‘unconscionable’ act
A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot and injured a man in New York City on Thursday afternoon during an enforcement operation, federal officials said.
The man was conscious and hospitalized, authorities said, and the shooting quickly sparked angry protests from local residents and elected officials in the neighborhood.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ICE agent shoots man in New York City with five-year-old reportedly in car

articles.author: Paul Daley
articles.description:
A proposal to livestream the killing of Nidal Hasan by firing squad opens a window ever wider to the Trump administration’s complete moral vacuity
More fool me! Here I was thinking nothing that America’s Trump administration could do or say, no matter how politically and morally bankrupt, no matter how venal or violent, was capable of shocking me any longer.
Then I woke to today’s news that one of the Trump cabinet’s bigger boofheads – the uber Christian nationalist, crusader-fantasist and “secretary of war” Pete Hegseth had announced that America would have a public firing squad execution of murderer Nidal Hasan.
Paul Daley is a Guardian Australia columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Execution TV? Pete Hegseth has taken the once ‘greatest democracy’ to a horrific new low | Paul Daley

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Amid a cost-of-living crisis, with US midterms a month away, the president held a ceremony to celebrate our tech overlords – again
He stands accused of being out of touch, enriching himself and his family, building a lavish White House ballroom and, with elections looming, neglecting the hardships of the voters who brought him to power.
Time for Donald Trump to show he still has the common touch? Nope.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump hosts awards party for tech billionaires, almost as if he doesn’t care about ordinary Americans

articles.author: Sam Levine in St Louis, Missouri
articles.description:
State residents express anger at Republicans who allowed chaotic voting maps saga to unfold ahead of the midterms

Sign up to The Stakes 2026: your weekly guide to the US midterms

Send us your questions on how the US economy is shaping the midterm elections

Eric Leventhal knows he’s going to vote for a Democrat in Congress when he goes to the polls in Missouri this November – the problem is he has no idea which candidate is going to be on his ballot.
In the state’s August primary, he voted for Fred Wellman, a Democrat running in the state’s second congressional district. But after a long and complicated legal battle sparked by Donald Trump’s desire to gain every advantage in the upcoming midterm contest, the districts have changed for the general election that will determine which party controls Congress. Leventhal said he lived right near the border of the first and second congressional district, so now he’s not sure which one he’s in.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Undistilled cheating’: Missouri voters furious in aftermath of Trump bid to rig electoral maps

articles.author: Nick Brown
articles.description:
A coalition of Democratic attorneys general is working to make sure voters across the spectrum have their voices heard
Elections have consequences. So do the Trump administration’s exhaustive efforts to undermine them.
Voters will be confident in their choices, but less certain whose voice will count in the face of myriad intrusions by the executive branch. A coalition of Democratic attorneys general are working to make sure voters across the political spectrum have their say.
Nick Brown is the attorney general of the state of Washington
 Continue reading...
articles.title: I’m the attorney general of Washington state. Here’s how we’re protecting the midterm elections | Nick Brown

articles.description:
Donald Trump’s latest campaign rally in San Antonio, Texas, was rocked by repeated protests as the US president urged Texas voters to back the embattled Senate candidate Ken Paxton. At least half a dozen demonstrators interrupted the US president during his speech, with some led away by police. One was physically assaulted by a Trump supporter as he tried to leave the arena. The Republican campaign to maintain control of the Senate has become increasingly focused on Texas, where the Democrat James Talarico has emerged as a serious threat
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Protesters removed after disrupting Trump rally in Texas – video

articles.author: Chris Stein in Lima, Ohio
articles.description:
Ohio former senator attacks Republican rival as the ‘face of datacenters’ as he wraps AI concerns into pro-worker message

Send us your questions on how the US economy is shaping the midterm elections

Sherrod Brown, the Democratic former senator from Ohio hoping to return to office in November’s midterm elections, has spent the past year traveling across his home state explaining to voters about all the ways the “system is rigged” against them. Recently, he’s been telling people about a trip he took across the north-west Ohio countryside.
“You’re driving on what looks like really good farmland, driving past fields, driving past barns, driving past milking parlors, and you see, all of a sudden, you see these huge cranes and you see these trucks coming,” Brown told a crowd of dozens at a coffee shop in the city of Lima earlier this month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘System is rigged’: Democrat Sherrod Brown puts datacenter danger at heart of populist Senate bid

articles.author: Shannon Heffernan and Anna Flagg of the Marshall Project
articles.description:
Children are being detained in record numbers, sometimes alone and where lawyers and family cannot find them
The image of immigration officers arresting five-year-old Liam Conejo Ramos – in a blue bunny hat and Spider-Man backpack – in January sparked outrage across the country.
Celebrities from Ms Rachel to Madonna called for the closure of the Dilley immigration processing center, the Texas immigrant camp that held Ramos and many children like him. Lawyers filed complaints about contaminated food and shoddy healthcare, and hundreds of activists protested outside the detention camp. Within months, the government began sending fewer children to Dilley.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Chaos and cruelty’: the kids trapped in Trump’s immigration enforcement campaign

articles.author: Margaret Sullivan
articles.description:
Trump seems to invent ugly new variations on his press-bashing theme almost every day
When you hate the mainstream press as much as Donald Trump does, nothing gets in the way of the punishment fantasy.
Not court rulings. Not public opinion. Not even the dreadful consequence of less media coverage.
Margaret Sullivan is a Guardian US columnist writing on media, politics and culture
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s latest attacks on the press exude desperation | Margaret Sullivan

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman with Charles Blow and Shrai Popat , produced by Tiara Chiaramonte , engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
The biggest question in US politics may be whether Democrats can ever win in the south. In this year’s midterms, Georgia has once again emerged as a bellwether. The state has shifted from deep red to purple for the last several election cycles and remains a frontline state in the battle over voting rights. In a recent Stateside with Kai and Carter live event in collaboration with On Air Presents, hosts Kai Wright and Carter Sherman were joined by Guardian contributing writer Charles Blow and political reporter Shrai Popat for a lively conversation about everything at stake in Georgia – including why Jon Ossoff needs Keisha Lance Bottoms to win the governor’s race if he hopes to run for president in 2028, what Donald Trump might do to intervene in the election, and how any voter suppression moves could backfire in the south.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Could Trump’s plan to suppress voters backfire in the south? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
Donald Trump’s unpopularity and the economic struggles of voters have boosted Democrats. But with less than a month to go, there is no complacency
For once, Democrats and Donald Trump might be in agreement: “Pretend I’m on the ticket,” the historically unpopular president has instructed supporters. Midterms are in large part a referendum on the incumbent, and Trump’s war on Iran and its impact on the cost of living have boosted support for Democrats. With less than a month to go, they have reason to be upbeat. The party has a mountain to climb after the devastating defeats of 2024, and the gerrymandering of Republicans, but surveys give it a lead of about nine points on the generic ballot, which measures preference for parties rather than specific candidates.
Attention has turned from the prospects of seizing the House, where Democrats are forecast a clear majority, to what once seemed like the highly optimistic possibility of taking the Senate too. That would require flipping four seats, with 35 in play. Remarkably, Democrats are prospering in red states from Texas to Alaska. In Kansas – which Mr Trump carried by 16 points, and which has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932 – the race is neck and neck.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on the US midterms: the cost of living is on the ballot, but this is about democracy too | Editorial

articles.author: Chris Stein, Alex Clark, Andrew Witherspoon and Ashley Kirk
articles.description:
These graphics explain what the Democrats would need to do to flip the Senate and House of Representatives
A turning point in Donald Trump’s second term will soon arrive. On 3 November, voters across the US will decide whether to keep the president’s Republican allies in control of Congress, or return Democrats to the majority.
Many indicators of voter sentiment suggest the Democrats are favored to take back control of the House of Representatives, and potentially the Senate. Winning either would be a significant victory for the party and give it the power to block Trump’s legislative agenda and more aggressively investigate his administration.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The US midterm races that will decide control of Congress – mapped

articles.author: Laure Boulinier, Sofia Couceiro and Boglarka Kosztolanyi
articles.description:
The US midterms may not be as much of a spectacle as the presidential elections, but they are just as important and can completely change not just the course of a presidential term, but federal legislation for years to come. The Guardian unpacks how these elections work, what the results mean and how they affect American life
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US midterms: what are they and why do presidents dread them? – explainer

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland with James Henson, produced by Nada Smiljanic and Danielle Stephens
articles.description:
Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico is surprising everyone, as polls have him leading his Republican opponent, Ken Paxton, in the Republican-led state of Texas.

Jonathan Freedland speaks to James Henson, founder and executive director of the Texas Politics Project, about why a blue wave in the Lone Star state would be seismic
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is James Talarico about to flip Texas for the Democrats? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow (now); Hamish Mackay and Adam Fulton (earlier)
articles.description:
Sagal Abdi-Wali defeats Green party leader Zack Polanski to retain the Holborn and St Pancras seat for Labour

Labour fends off Green party to win Holborn and St Pancras byelection

Activists in Camden have suggested the Greens’ decision to back the anti-Zionism motion has cost them votes in the byelection.
Councillors for both Labour the Liberal Democrats told the Press Association that voters had informed them they would not be backing the Green party after it passed the motion last weekend calling Zionism racism.
It is clear now we will come a close second in this by-election. Taking the fight to Labour in one of its safest seats shows just how far the Greens have come.
Voters want us to keep Labour’s feet to the fire on affordable housing, public ownership of water and the climate crisis. Greens will be there every single day, holding Labour to account and demanding the change people voted for.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour wins Holborn and St Pancras byelection; Polanski ‘absolutely’ intends to remain Green party leader – UK politics live

articles.author: Denis Campbell
articles.description:
Decision by Royal College of Pharmacy to end sponsorship comes after concerns over Teva Pharmaceuticals’ ‘activities’
A second major UK health body has cut ties with an Israeli drug firm after coming under pressure from pro-Palestine campaigners.
The Royal College of Pharmacy has dropped Teva UK, the British arm of the global medicines producer Teva Pharmaceuticals, as a sponsor of and exhibitor at its annual conference next month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Second UK health body drops Israeli drug firm after activist pressure

articles.author: Rachel Salvidge
articles.description:
Exclusive: Firms made more than £340m last year from processing industrial and commercial wastewater at sewage works that are unable to remove many chemical pollutants
Water companies in the UK made more than £340m in revenue last year by pouring billions of litres of industrial and commercial wastewater into sewage treatment works that experts say are not designed to remove most chemicals, leaving pollutants to pass into rivers, seas and farmland.
Water companies are required by law to take industrial wastewater and issue permits called “trade-effluent consents” that allow businesses to send it to sewage works, though water companies can refuse applications.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Revealed: the ‘black box’ wastewater trade that rakes in millions for UK utility companies

articles.author: Sammy Gecsoyler
articles.description:
Victory by Sagal Abdi-Wali in north London seat will be a relief for Andy Burnham in high-stakes battle for the left of British politics

Holborn and St Pancras byelection – live updates


Labour has seen off the Greens to win the Holborn and St Pancras byelection in a result that will relieve Andy Burnham and dent Zack Polanski’s position as a decisive power player on the left of British politics.
The byelection, called after former prime minister Keir Starmer resigned from the seat in September, was considered a two-horse race between the Labour candidate, Sagal Abdi-Wali, and the Green party leader, Polanski. Abdi-Wali received 12,292 votes, 45% of the vote, to Polanski’s 8,928, 33% of the vote.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour fends off Green party to win Holborn and St Pancras byelection

articles.author: Denis Campbell and Anna Bawden
articles.description:
England-focused mental health review returns stark warning and calls for shift to ‘needs-led’ system

Explainer | What has the Fonagy review found and what does it recommend?

Analysis | No ‘snowflakes’: mental health review says today’s youth have it harder and harms are real

The NHS in England is heading into a “world of system failures” as it struggles to cope with relentlessly rising demand for mental health, ADHD and autism care, leaving those affected desperate for support, a government-commissioned inquiry has found.
The stark warning was made in a review led by Prof Peter Fonagy into the sharp rise in demand over recent decades for help with mental health and neurodevelopmental conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NHS at risk of ‘system failures’ as demand for ADHD and autism care soars, inquiry finds

articles.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
articles.description:
Peter Fonagy lauds courage of young people and warns of consequences of rising prevalence of mental illness

Full report | NHS at risk of ‘system failures’ as demand for ADHD and autism care soars, inquiry finds

Explainer | What has the Fonagy review found and what does it recommend?

Eighteen months ago, in an off-the-cuff remark during a discussion on disability benefit cuts, Wes Streeting said mental health conditions were being “overdiagnosed”, riding headlong into another culture war.
He later apologised for the comment, but at the time it seemed the then health secretary had endorsed a populist view that ordinary stresses and disappointments had become too often medicalised, resulting in a surge of bogus clinical diagnoses and creating a “snowflake generation” of fragile, avoidant and workshy young people.
I am in awe of their courage. Young people are contending with more powerful forces than I ever faced
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No ‘snowflakes’: mental health review says today’s youth have it harder and harms are real

articles.author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Prof Peter Fonagy’s 607-page report is categoric that mental distress has increased substantially and ‘cannot be explained by greater awareness alone’

Full report | NHS at risk of ‘system failures’ as demand for ADHD and autism care soars, inquiry finds

Analysis | No ‘snowflakes’: mental health review says today’s youth have it harder and harms are real

The Fonagy review of NHS England’s mental health, ADHD and autism services was commissioned in 2025 by Wes Streeting, then the health secretary, in response to growing concerns that spiralling waiting lists for assessment, diagnosis and care threatened the NHS’s ability to meet the demand.
The 607-page report, published on Friday, says that without a radical overhaul, mental health and neurodiversity services will be overwhelmed. Here are some of its key findings and recommendations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NHS England mental health services review: what has it found and what does it recommend?

articles.author: Richard Adams Education editor
articles.description:
Nine in 10 school heads who responded say inspections still ‘negatively affected’ staff mental health
School inspections in England continue to damage the mental wellbeing of teachers and senior leaders, according to a survey commissioned by Ofsted that casts doubt on efforts to reduce the stress caused by inspectors’ visits.
The independent survey of school leaders who had undergone the revised inspections since last year found that 88% said it had “negatively affected” the mental wellbeing of school staff, including 29% who said it affected them “a lot”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Ofsted inspection regime damaging teachers, survey says

articles.author: Aletha Adu and Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Contest seen as test of Andy Burnham’s ability to unite Labour voters amid threat from Green party’s Zack Polanski
Polls have closed in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection, a contest seen as a test of whether Andy Burnham can unite Labour’s voters or whether Zack Polanski can peel off support from the party’s progressive flank.
Labour is seeking to retain Keir Starmer’s former north London seat, where he won a majority of more than 11,000 votes in the 2024 general election.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Polls close in Holborn and St Pancras byelection as Labour hopes to retain seat

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Men aged 32 and 36 detained on suspicion of trespass, causing criminal damage and entering a prohibited place 
Two Latvian men were arrested in the early hours of Thursday after they were discovered inside the perimeter of RAF Molesworth, a Cambridgeshire base used by the US military and Nato for intelligence operations.
The men, 32 and 36, were picked up at 2am inside the base, in an investigation that began four hours earlier when military police discovered an abandoned vehicle outside the facility.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two Latvian men arrested at RAF base in Cambridgeshire used by US military

articles.author: Ben Quinn
articles.description:
Intelligence specialist Teddy Young, 24, alleged to have drafted message in Russian containing classified information
A junior Royal Navy intelligence specialist from Bedfordshire accused of trying to pass military secrets to Russia appeared in court on Thursday.
Teddy Young, 24, was accused of abusing his high-level security clearance to access secret defence and intelligence data after being deployed on a warship.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Royal Navy sailor accused of spying for Russia appears in court

articles.author: Esther Addley
articles.description:
Inquest hears details of how three women spent their final days but why they ended their lives may never be known
Jane Adetoro and her younger sisters, Christina and Rebecca Walters, were “the closest sisters and the best friends”, according to their family. Devoted to their father, Joseph, whom they messaged every day, the adult siblings lived quiet lives in the flat they shared in west London and would do everything together.
When they died in May this year, it was no different. Early in the morning of 13 May, the sisters’ bodies were recovered from the sea in Brighton, hours after a taxi had dropped the three women at the beachfront.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A lake pilgrimage and a quiet car ride to the beach: last hours of sisters who took own lives in Brighton

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Closure will cost at least 60 jobs, while Leeds and Bristol outlets to be converted to Flannels brand
Harvey Nichols’ Birmingham store is to close in January, with the loss of at least 60 jobs, while its Leeds and Bristol outlets will be converted to the Flannels brand in a shake-up under Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group.
The owner of Sports Direct bought the department store chain, whose headquarters are at the Knightsbridge site in London, for £43m on the day it was put into administration in mid-August.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Harvey Nichols’ Birmingham store to close in January

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Consulate targeted in sanctions spat has unusual diplomatic status that clashes with Israel’s ambitions to fully annex the city
Israel’s attempt to close the British consulate general in Jerusalem was primarily designed to deter London from imposing sanctions on settlements in occupied Palestine. But it also served the current government’s ambitions to fully annex Jerusalem as a national capital, diplomatic and legal experts said.
The UK mission to the city has an unusual diplomatic status, which dates back to before the founding of the state of Israel, rooted in a vision of Jerusalem as a neutral enclave under international control.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel’s downgrading of UK consulate aims to tighten its hold on Jerusalem

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose
articles.description:
Complaints risks putting defence ministry on collision course with Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
The Ministry of Defence has objected to at least four planned windfarms in the past year over fears the spinning blades could cause “unacceptable interference” with radars used to detect military aircraft.
MoD officials raised concerns in late June over plans for an onshore windfarm in County Durham that could result in aircraft “not being detected” within an RAF Low Flying Area, according to a letter to Britain’s planning authority.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MoD has objected to four windfarms in past year over radar interference fears

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
UK and Israel back away from full diplomatic confrontation, though British presence in Palestine will be much reduced
Israel and the UK have backed away from a full-scale diplomatic confrontation, with Britain announcing it is rebranding its consulate general ⁠building in ⁠East Jerusalem ​as a UK mission, a move that will result in UK diplomats leaving Israel, with only seven to remain in the building. Among those leaving is the consul general, Helen Winterton.
The change was forced on the UK by the Israeli government as punishment for the decision by the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, last month to ban trade with illegal settlements and introduce a tougher sanctions regime against those who aided the building of settlements. The UK is seeking to protect the two-state solution as the best means of ending the Israel-Palestine conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British consulate in East Jerusalem will stay open as UK mission, says Ed Miliband

articles.author: Heather Stewart and Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Andrew Bailey tells chancellor ‘whatever the stance of fiscal policy, it must be credible and be seen as such by financial markets’
The Bank of England governor, Andrew Bailey, has urged the chancellor, John Healey, to agree a budget that reassures financial markets after the UK’s medium-term borrowing costs hit a fresh 19-year high.
With investors offloading government bonds previously considered safe havens amid fears of rising inflation, Bailey told all governments caught in the crosshairs of financial speculators that they needed to avoid market turmoil that raises the interest paid on debt.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bank governor urges John Healey to use budget to allay market fears amid bond turmoil

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Letter to government says changes will unfairly remove legal protections for children in England

Letter: Legal rights must be retained for children with Send

Campaigners are calling on Andy Burnham to abandon the core elements of the government’s overhaul of special educational needs provision in England, arguing they unfairly remove children’s legal protections.
A group of children, parents and experts, led by the broadcaster Chris Packham, have written a letter calling for the prime minister to gut the plans laid out under his predecessor Keir Starmer.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Campaigners led by Chris Packham urge prime minister to rethink Send overhaul

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Thinking Allowed, The Artificial Human and Free Thinking among other programmes hit by £500m cuts
BBC Radio 4’s consumer rights show You and Yours is to be axed after more than 50 years, becoming one of the latest victims of the corporation’s £500m cuts plan.
The programme, once described by the former Radio 4 controller Mark Damazer as “one of the most important” on the station, is one of a handful to be cut as the BBC searches for shows that can be more easily adapted as podcasts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: BBC axes long-running Radio 4 show You and Yours in push towards podcasts

articles.author: Taz Ali and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
Voters choosing replacement for Keir Starmer, who announced he was standing down last month
The UK’s military is too focused on global commitments at the expense of domestic defence, meaning the government’s planned increase in defence spending is likely to result in even greater waste, a thinktank report has warned.
According to an analysis by researchers at the Transition Security Project, Britain has the most overseas-oriented military among European nations, with almost a quarter of the defence budget spent on commitments across five continents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK politics: Polls open in Holborn and St Pancras byelection – as it happened

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Court hears former justice minister Shahid Malik had only ‘very limited’ role in business that made £6.67m in three weeks
A former Labour MP and justice minister has been found not guilty of charges around his role in a fraudulent Covid-19 testing company.
Shahid Malik, 58, was MP for Dewsbury between 2005 and 2010 and served as a minister in three departments in Gordon Brown’s government.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Former Labour MP cleared over role in fraudulent Covid-19 testing company

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Experts say breadth of data accessed could help attackers devise “highly convincing” phishing scams
Asos hackers gained access to millions of customers’ recent search histories as well as names, addresses and phone numbers, the online fashion retailer has revealed.
Terms typed in by customers such as “glamorous wide fit” and “Asos petite” were in the data accessed in the cyber-attack, which emerged on Tuesday after app users received a notification titled “Asos hacked” with a link to the Telegram messaging service.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Asos says customers’ names, contact details and search histories hacked

articles.author: Chris Osuh and Aamna Mohdin
articles.description:
Offences targeting Muslims increased most in 12 months to March – up 15% – while antisemitic hate crimes rose by 10%
Racially and religiously motivated offences have reached record highs in the UK as the government’s main Islamophobia partner says attacks on mosques are increasing in severity.
Home Office figures show police recorded 146,825 hate crimes in the year ending March 2026 – a rise of 7% in the past year. Offences targeting Muslims increased the most – up 15%, from 4,479 to 5,132, while antisemitic hate crimes rose by 10%, from 2,874 to 3,162.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Racial and religious hate crimes at record high in England and Wales, data shows

articles.author: Michael Cragg
articles.description:
Ymarfer Byw, which was praised for its ‘musical excellence’, beat 14 other albums to the prize of £10,000
Singer-songwriter Dafydd Owain has won the 2026 Welsh music prize with his second album Ymarfer Byw.
The emotionally charged record, which also won Welsh language album of the year in August, beat albums by the likes of Gruff Rhys, the Royston Club and Art School Girlfriend to the prize of £10,000.
ADJUA – Everything Is Beautiful
Aleighcia Scott – Taith
Ani Glass – Phantasmagoria
Art School Girlfriend – Lean In
Cerys Hafana – Angel
Chroma – 25 Forever
Dafydd Owain – Ymarfer Byw

Devastating blaze near Sizewell B nuclear power station in Suffolk among a record 624 wildfires in July this year
This July was the worst on record for wildfires in England, provisional data shows, with England experiencing a clear upward trend in the total number of wildfires recorded.
This summer has been a stark reminder of the vulnerability of the UK to climate breakdown, after punishingly hot and dry weather turned large parts of the countryside into a tinderbox.

articles.description:
Nine out of 10 people felt motivated to act after watching film outlining threats to food security, economy and public health
The British government must be honest about the scale of the threat posed by climate and nature breakdown, researchers have said, after nine out of 10 people surveyed after watching a briefing on the issue felt more motivated to act.
Last November, in the “first-of-its-kind national emergency briefing”, nine experts gave stark assessments in Central Hall in Westminster of the scale of the changes needed in the UK to adapt to the rapidly changing climate and ecological landscape.

articles.title: Britons kept in dark about scale of climate crisis, say viewers of ‘first-of-its-kind’ emergency briefing

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
Operation on 19-year-old who had no sperm after chemotherapy offers hope of preserving children’s fertility after cancer treatment 
Surgeons have performed the first testicular tissue transplant on a teenager in the UK, offering hope that boys left infertile by chemotherapy could one day have biological children.
The 19-year-old had his tissue removed and frozen three years ago before undergoing treatment for a serious blood disorder. He said he was “incredibly grateful” to the medical team behind the pioneering procedure, which represents a potential breakthrough for male fertility preservation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Teenager becomes first person to have testicular tissue transplant in UK

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
Hundred-and-fifty-year-old Wych elm in Newcastle, Co Down, has grown sideways owing to strong winds
The “astonishing and bizarre” Bendy Tree in Northern Ireland has been crowned the winner of this year’s tree of the year competition.
The wych elm tree, located in Newcastle, County Down, owes its name to its near horizontal trunk, which has grown sideways owing to the strong seaside winds coming off the Irish Sea.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bendy elm still standing against all odds crowned UK tree of the year

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Ethan Scott Brown died after being wrongly told he would not be eligible to graduate from the University of Glasgow 
The family of a student who took his own life after being wrongly told he would not be eligible to graduate have said the University of Glasgow “will be held to account”.
Ethan Scott Brown, 23, was due to graduate in December 2024 after studying geography.

articles.author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
articles.description:
The Tory leader’s proposal to slash the tax would shovel £6bn of taxpayer money to the already-wealthy
Kemi Badenoch’s inheritance tax gambit is a Conservative classic. After all, it was George Osborne’s high-profile pledge to “take the family home out of inheritance tax” in 2007 that put Gordon Brown off calling a snap general election.
In practice, Osborne’s plan involved a £1m threshold for inheritance tax – and given the global financial crisis had blown a hole in the public finances by the time the Conservative-Lib Dem coalition came to power in 2010, it never came to pass.

articles.title: Badenoch’s inheritance tax gambit makes no economic sense | Heather Stewart

Pennon slashes dividend and launches £550m cash call ‘to drive improved outcomes for customers and communities’

Burnham, take note: water shareholders have their uses

The owner of embattled South West Water has slashed its dividend and launched a cash call to investors as it attempts to fund infrastructure investment, days after it was hit by a record £7.9m fine for hundreds of sewage spills.
London-listed Pennon said on Wednesday it would tap investors for £550m, as part of a £1bn investment “to drive improved outcomes for customers and communities”.

articles.author: Eve Livingston
articles.description:
Scots-written Till the Bells Ring  premiered a year before the Hollywood film, which featured spoken words by Al Jolson
For almost a century, The Jazz Singer has been celebrated as the world’s first feature-length film to include synchronised dialogue (known as a “talkie”), and English as the first language of cinema. But a chance discovery threatens to upend film history with the news that it may have been beaten to the title by a full year – and by a film made in Glasgow and written in Scots.
The breakthrough was made by the historian and self-confessed “film nerd” Marc David Jacobs, who was conducting research for a book on the first wave of British sound films when he came across the story of Till the Bells Ring.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scottish film could steal The Jazz Singer’s crown as ‘world’s first talkie’

articles.author: Matthew Taylor
articles.description:
‘Techno-optimism’ may lead to reliance on unproven solutions at expense of societal changes needed
Scientists who believe technology will largely solve the problems caused by the climate crisis are less likely to engage in civic action on the issue, according to a study.
The report from the London School of Economics found they are 23% less likelyto sign petitions or take part in protests than peers who doubt that technology is the answer. They are also 18% less likely to make high-impact lifestyle changes, from reducing flights to changing to a vegan or vegetarian diet.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scientists who put faith in technology less likely to take climate action

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Exclusive: 10-year sponsorship extension at a 50% premium on last agreement crowns bonanza year for live venue
O2 has struck a record deal thought to be in the region of £200m to retain the naming rights to the London venue the O2 in the largest renewal of its kind in UK history.
The 10-year agreement will extend O2’s relationship until at least 2038. It cements the sponsorship as the second longest-running UK stadium naming rights deal after Arsenal’s partnership for the football club’s London ground,
 Continue reading...
articles.title: O2 signs record deal to keep London venue’s naming rights

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
More than 1 million people in Great Britain now vape despite having never regularly smoked, ONS data shows
More than 1 million people in Great Britain now vape despite never having been regular smokers, with rates nearly doubling in just four years, according to figures that health experts describe as concerning.
About 5.4 million people aged 16 and above in England, Scotland and Wales (9.9%) used e-cigarettes daily or occasionally in 2025, Office for National Statistics data showed. Vaping was highest among those aged 25-34 (16.4%).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Proportion of people in Great Britain vaping who never smoked doubles in four years
